newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GASCOIGNE BACK IN ENGLAND SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GASCOIGNE BACK IN ENGLAND SQUAD.

text.p: The irrespressible Paul Gascoigne reclaimed his place in the England squad on Friday as manager Glenn Hoddle bolstered his attacking midfield for a World Cup qualifier against Poland and four friendlies in the next five weeks.
Gascoigne missed England's last three matches with an ankle injury and did not return to the Glasgow Rangers side until late April when he came on as a substitute.
Hoddle left him out of the squad for England's 2-0 defeat of Georgia in a World Cup qualifier nine days ago because Gascoigne lacked match fitness.
But the inspirational midfielder returns for a series of fixtures which should help define the shape of a potential England squad for the World Cup finals in 1998.
England play South Africa in a friendly on May 24, a week before they face Poland away in a European group two World Cup qualifier.
They then play Brazil, France and group rival Italy in a friendly tournament in France in early June.
Hoddle said Gascoigne, who has had a torrid year off the pitch and an injury-marred season on it, still had work to do before he returned to his brilliant best.
"He's got to get back to loving the game of football again," Hoddle told a news conference. "He needs to do a bit more work from now, he needs to work on his fitness.
"When he was back in his heyday, when he was at his best, I think you could see he was enjoying the game. That's when it becomes a labour of love."
Hoddle said Gascoigne could still feature at the heart of the England midfield next year when they hope to qualify for the World Cup finals.
"He wants to put his game back together again," Hoddle said. "He's 30 years old and with that talent he could be playing until he's 37."
Arsenal's Paul Merson and Manchester United's Paul Scholes were the other attacking midfielders drafted in to the 27-man squad.
Merson has recently recovered from a hernia operation. Scholes is called up for the first time.
Goalkeepers - Tim Flowers (Blackburn), Nigel Martyn (Leeds), David Seaman (Arsenal)

Defenders - Gary Neville (Manchester United), Graeme Le Saux (Blackburn), Gareth Southgate (Aston Villa), Tony Adams (Arsenal), Sol Campbell (Tottenham), Gary Pallister (Manchester United), Martin Keown (Arsenal), Stuart Pearce (Nottingham Forest), Philip Neville (Manchester United)

Midfielders - Paul Ince (Inter Milan), David Beckham (Manchester United), Steve McManaman (Liverpool), David Batty (Newcastle), Robert Lee (Newcastle), Jamie Redknapp (Liverpool), Paul Gascoigne (Glasgow Rangers), Paul Scholes (Manchester United), Paul Merson (Arsenal), Nicky Butt (Manchester United)
Strikers - Robbie Fowler (Liverpool), Ian Wright (Arsenal), Teddy Sheringham (Tottenham), Alan Shearer (Newcastle), Les Ferdinand (Newcastle).
